title: Alpine Bridge pilot outreach spark notes
content:
Quick gist:
- Alpine Bridge (mid-market retail SaaS) — headless commerce + personalization layer. Good pilot candidate: same customers as other retail pilots but smaller footprint, cares about latency and vendor lock-in.
- Goal: 6-week pilot to prove support deflection via AI chat + improved product search relevance with lightweight reranker.

Notes from research (public + paid):
- HQ: Portland; ~120 employees; Series C 2023; strong retail vertical focus (outdoor gear).
- Recent funding used for expanding B2B platform and merchant success org.
- Tech stack: Shopify Plus for storefronts, Snowflake analytics, Segment, custom Node/K8s backend. Uses Intercom for support.
- Signals of intent: job posting for "Head of ML" (Priya Singh) — mentions embeddings for product search; PR about improving checkout UX last quarter.
- Champions to look for: Evan Moreno (Head of Product), Priya Singh (Head of ML), Dana Ruiz (Head of Merchant Success).

Why Redwood matters for Alpine Bridge (short):
- Low-friction pilot via Hosted API to move fast, then Dedicated if predictability matters.
- Observable cost + latency breakdowns so engineering can justify migration off current MTurk-ish rerankers.
- Prefix/KV caching and smart batching can reduce token cost on chat + product descriptions at scale.
- Private/VPC option for enterprise merchants who require data residency.

Pilot hypothesis and scope (6 weeks):
- Week 0: onboarding + data sync (product catalog + 30 days of support transcripts).
- Week 1–2: embed generation for product catalog + simple nearest-neighbor search. Create baseline recall/precision metrics.
- Week 3–4: reranker model (server-side) to boost top-5 conversion intent relevance; A/B test on a 5% traffic slice.
- Week 5–6: conversational support agent (Intercom integration) for common refunds/returns flows and order-tracking — measure deflection rate.
- Success criteria: +8% conversion on search queries where reranker applied OR >20% support deflection on automated flows; P95 latency < 300ms for rerank calls; predictable cost <= $X per 100k queries (TBD).

Outbound sequence (short templates) — personalization hooks based on research:
- Email 1 (cold): Subject: beta pilot for catalog search + cheaper chat
  Hi Evan —
  Saw Priya’s job post mentioning embeddings and search. We recently ran a 6‑week pilot with a footwear platform that saw a +9% lift in product relevance using a lightweight reranker and saved ~$2.8k/mo in inference spend after caching.
  Would you be open to a 20‑min sync to see if a similar scoped pilot makes sense for Alpine Bridge?
  —Sofia

- LinkedIn note (short):
  Hi Evan — curious if you’re exploring embeddings for search. We help teams run pilots in weeks (hosted -> dedicated -> private). Happy to share a short case study.

- Follow-up call script bullets:
  - Quick intros (2m)
  - Confirm existing search pain: mismatched results, manual boosting, cost issues (3m)
  - Show quick architecture: feed -> embedding store -> reranker -> client (4m)
  - Pilot ask & timeline (3m)

Objection handling (raw / quick replies):
- "We don’t want vendor lock-in / security risk":
  - Short: we can run the pilot on Hosted API and demonstrate data controls; for production we offer Dedicated pools or Private VPC + KMS. We have SOC2 + enterprise controls and can sign an NDA quickly.
- "Latency sounds risky for search":
  - Short: reranker calls are small (short contexts). We hit P95 <300ms in similar pilots using batching and KV cache — we’ll instrument and share dashboards.
- "Cost is unpredictable":
  - Short: start with a fixed-scope pilot and telemetry — use our Optimize recommendations (quantize/shorten contexts, cache prefixes) to bound costs. We can model expected spend from first 10k queries.
- "Quality varies between models":
  - Short: we’ll run side-by-side evaluations on your query set and threshold rollout; also automatic fallback to earlier model when regressions detected.

KPIs & instrumentation (what to measure):
- Search: CTR on top 3 results, add-to-cart rate per query, search-to-order conversion, mean reciprocal rank (MRR).
- Support: % of Intercom conversations deflected, average time saved per agent, tickets/year reduced.
- Infra: P95 latency, tokens per request, inference $/100k queries.

Internal next actions (owners):
- Outreach: send first cold email to Evan + Priya (Sofia) — target week of 2025-02-10.
- Demo assets: prepare 5-min rerank demo using sample catalog (Liam). Create short GIF for email.
- Security pack: assemble SOC2 + DPA summary + basic SSO/KMS notes for quick send (Aisha).
- Ticket: create sales play ticket JIRA-7189 (pilot-opportunity) and link to Confluence page.

Risky unknowns / open questions:
- Will merchants allow product catalog export for embedding? (some will require scoping)
- Intercom access level required for deep integration — need commerce/ops contact.
- Cost target: what is their acceptable $/month for support automation — need Dana’s input.

Possible success story angle (for marketing):
- "How Alpine Bridge cut support tickets by 30% and improved search relevance with a 6-week inference pilot" — include metrics, tech choices, and cost breakdown.

Quick drafts for email follow-ups (short):
- Email 2 (if no response): Subject: quick question on search pilot
  Evan — following up. Quick ask: do you have a subset of merchant stores we could pilot on (5–10)? If yes I’ll send a short doc with next steps and data checklist.

- Email 3 (if engaged): Subject: pilot scope & timeline
  Thanks for the time — attached is a 1-page pilot scope (data needed, timeline, roles). If that looks good we can kick off next week.

Meeting agenda (1st call) — 20 minutes:
- Intros & goals (3m)
- Pain confirmation & current flow (5m)
- Proposed pilot architecture & timelines (7m)
- Next steps & decision checkpoints (5m)

Notes to self (tone: informal):
- Keep it light — they’re skeptical of vendors after a bad GenAI vendor experience. Focus on small scoped win.
- Bring concrete numbers (latency/cost) from recent retail pilot — Liam has the runbook.
- Prep a one-page data checklist (only product csv + 30d transcripts) to remove friction.

End of scratch notes.
summary: Scratchpad for Alpine Bridge retail pilot — account research, pilot scope, outbound templates, objections, KPIs, and next steps.
